content:
I'm excited to share doc-verification-bridge, a documentation tool for Lean 4 that automatically extracts verification relationships from your code—no annotations required.

What it does: For each theorem/lemma, it identifies:

  • What definitions it assumes as preconditions
  • What it proves properties about
  • What Bool functions it validates (bridging theorems connecting decidable code to Prop specs)
  • What other theorems/lemmas it depends on (extracted from proof terms)

Why it matters: Proof assistants guarantee theorems are correct, but don't help answer "which theorems verify this function?" or "what assumptions does this proof rely on?" This tool closes that gap.

Key features:

  • Integrates with doc-gen4 for unified documentation
  • Scales to Mathlib4 (280K+ declarations analyzed)
  • Classifies declarations using a four-category ontology (mathematical vs computational, types vs definitions)

:document: Paper submitted to NFM 2026: "What theorems assume, prove, validate, and depend on?"

:link: Project: https://github.com/NicolasRouquette/doc-verification-bridge

:www: Generated docs (16 projects, including Batteries, FLT, PhysLean, and Mathlib4): https://nicolasrouquette.github.io/doc-verification-bridge

Feedback welcome! I'd love to collaborate with the community on improving the classification heuristics and exploring integration with doc-gen4.

Thanks to @Henrik Böving for reviewing and merging a couple of PRs that made this integration possible!
